clinician.final_diagnosis: cblC deficiency associated with anti-factor H antibody-associated hemolytic uremic syndrome
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 19-year-old woman presented with asthenia, dyspnea, hypertension, and lower limb edema, progressing to acute kidney failure and severe neurologic impairment. Initial labs showed microangiopathic hemolytic anemia with schistocytes, elevated LDH, low haptoglobin, heavy proteinuria and hematuria, and negative direct antiglobulin test. Complement factors were normal and no complement gene mutations were found, but she had a high anti-factor H antibody titer. Metabolic testing revealed markedly elevated plasma homocysteine and significant methylmalonic aciduria. Kidney biopsy demonstrated thrombotic microangiopathy features including mesangial sclerosis, GBM duplication, and thrombi with mild IgM and C3 deposits. Genetic sequencing identified two heterozygous pathogenic variants in the MMACHC gene confirming cblC deficiency. These findings fully support the diagnosis of cblC deficiency associated with anti-factor H antibody-associated hemolytic uremic syndrome.
